objective: Test the owner's picture of time as a pattern and as a priority. Write the added rules for one birth at a time, with nothing that reads a next round, and run them on the rings that return under complete rounds, on cycles through dead knots and on the record's eight-knot clock with and without its attachments: in every order of a bounded opening, in sampled fair orders, and under four named priorities. First discriminator: whether the structure built by the first returns depends on the order. Also each clock's returns per birth as more is attached to it. Stop at a priority read from the structure under which the result does not depend on ties and a loaded clock is slower per birth, or at the smallest start on which every registered rule and priority builds something different; in either case with every frozen prediction given a verdict.
title: No round supplied: does the ring still return one birth at a time, in every order and under priorities read from the structure?
